context:
Restore the specific guidance with the per-platform service counts stated
explicitly, and add a machine-checkable assertion so the claim cannot drift from
the compose files it describes.
description:
Commit fd29aa77c0 compressed a specific, actionable mocker caveat into vague
text. The original read, in substance: multi-service stacks are NOT validated --
databend stays healthy on docker but its minio service exits on mocker, so use
docker for multi-service; doris and starrocks are all-in-one single containers
and are fine.

AGENTS.md now says only that mocker is local-only and unsuitable for certain
cases. On 2026-08-04 that wording caused an agent to assert that doris and
starrocks were the known-bad multi-service case and to plan around a constraint
that does not exist. The user corrected it three times before the original text
was recovered by git archaeology. Verified against the compose files: databend
has 3 services, doris 1, starrocks 1.

anti_patterns.dont: compress this again in a future canonicalization pass without checking what the specifics were
anti_patterns.instead: keep the detail in the operator guide, which canonicalization does not compress
anti_patterns.why: fd29aa77c0 lost operational detail that cost a session to recover

anti_patterns.instead: name the platform and the service that fails
anti_patterns.why: that is the false claim the compression produced; the validated failure is specific to databend's minio service

anti_patterns.dont: restore the guidance as prose only
anti_patterns.instead: state the counts and add a test asserting them
anti_patterns.why: prose is exactly what drifted; the service counts it asserts are checkable from the compose files

preserves.behavior: AGENTS.md remains the active authority and stays concise; the detail lives in the operator guide with AGENTS.md pointing at it.
No change to container engine resolution behavior.

prior_art.concept: line 147 currently carries the compressed wording; restore specificity in place rather than adding a second mocker section elsewhere
operator guide already documents container engine resolution; the detailed mocker caveats belong here with AGENTS.md pointing at it
